sourceFindings.finding: CAP Table 5 requires concurrent IHC and specified review for uncommon ISH groups. The existing HER2 owner already integrates these; the exercise supplies a completed negative interpretation.
The Loi 2019 pooled diagnostic-sample association concerns early TNBC treated with specified chemotherapy; it is not individual outcome certainty or proof of added pembrolizumab benefit.
A BRCA finding alone does not satisfy the early-breast indication or OlympiA high-risk criteria. The trial included hormone receptor-positive participants as well as TNBC.
CREATE-X and OlympiA supply specific comparisons; OlympiA disallowed post-neoadjuvant capecitabine. Neither should silently become a different post-pembrolizumab or head-to-head comparison.

sourceFindings.finding: The previous grade/stage/receptor lead promised receptor-defined drug response, treatment intensity and a fixed biopsy/surgery reporting order. The replacement distinguishes measurements, staging contexts and conditional treatment evidence.

sourceFindings.status: corrected in biopsy lead and summary consumers
sourceFindings.finding: The previous generic biopsy lead claimed it was the only way to confirm any cancer. The current lead describes the procedure and specimen limits; eight stale unreviewed translations are withdrawn and Simple English corrected.

One old TIL XML was a BioC error page and another metadata only. Fresh EPMC fullTextXML failed, NCBI initially returned 429, and readable PMC HTML ultimately supplied the targeted denominator. No false full-text credit.
The 2019 CTNeoBC and 2025 NRG-BR005 erratum bodies were not read. They are not certified reconciled, and no new numerical claims depend on guessing their scope.

CAP ER Table 2 displays an overlapping 10% boundary in its Positive and Low Positive rows; the adjacent prose and 2020 guideline specify the 1% to 10% ER-low category. The 5% exercise is unambiguous; no new 10% boundary rule is invented.
